main_text.p: «Cùm venissent autem in Myfiam; tentabant «ire in Bithyniam: & non permisit illis Spiritus «Jesu. Quid autem mirum,si, inter ipsa praedi-«cationis Evangelicae exordia, non poterant «ire Apostoli; nisi quò eos Dei Spiritus ire vo-«luisset: cùm videamus, plerasque gentes modò «primùm Christianæ gratiæ fieri cœpisse partici-«pes; alias autem nullum adhuc odorem boni «istius attigisse? An dicendum est; voluntati «Dei humanas obsistere voluntates? & tam fe-«ros, tamq; intractabiles hominum mores; ut «Evangelium ideò non audiant, quia praedica-«tioni impia corda non pateant? Et quis istis «(prioribus obsequentibus) corda muta-«vit; nisi qui finxit sigillatim corda eorum? &c.

Atque ex his, quæ repetuntur in eandem sententiam, lib.1.de vocat. Gent.c. 12.& 2.cap.2. intelligitur; quo sensu, ut ait Grotius, repetat: non negādum, quin & velit Deus omnes homines salvos fieri; & tamen non omnes salvi fiant. videlicet non, ut ipse explicat, (credo, ex Damasceno, lib. 2. de orthod. fid. cap. 29.) κατὰ τὴν θέλησιν τὴν προηγυμένην (nequedum enim illa tunc nata erat, eo sensu, distinctio) sed

page.notes: Quotation marks at the start of each line of the quoted passage are printed as double quotes and are shown as «. The Greek phrase is read with doubt; the second word of the Greek phrase is uncertain (the scan shows a blurred form, probably προηγουμένην). Italic passages were identified by letter shape and may be incomplete. The catchword "sed" stands at the lower right and is also the start of the next page, so it is kept as catchword only.
